summary: English and Dari first-party discovery identified Afghanistan's official land-affairs/cadastral custodian and official Badakhshan cadastral survey activity. The inspected public pages expose no anonymous parcel map/API, parcel schema, CRS, or safe ID-plus-geometry response. No geometry sample was retained.
queryAndRequestOutcomes: All executed discovery queries, URLs, direct requests, current HTML/JavaScript inspection, schema/CRS checks, safe field allowlist, scope limits, and uncertainty are recorded in city-4917-fayzabad.json. No login, CAPTCHA/Cloudflare bypass, credentials, private tokens, TLS bypass, unsafe-field request, or formal land-record submission occurred.

custodians.name: Afghanistan land-affairs authority, General Directorate of Geodesy, Cadastre and Deeds
custodians.scope: National custodian evidenced by its official land-affairs description.

custodians.name: Badakhshan provincial land-affairs/cadastral administration
custodians.scope: Provincial cadastral activity evidenced by official survey-and-mapping reports; no separate public Fayzabad service or parcel layer was found.

safeFieldAllowlist: stable native cadastral parcel identifier only if source-proven
full parcel polygon geometry only when safely returned
scopeLimits: The exact WUP point and population are preserved in the city record.
Badakhshan survey activity is not evidence of public vector coverage or citywide parcel availability.
No exact-point lookup was possible without a qualified anonymous endpoint; access/qualification limits are not parcel absence.
No unsafe land-record fields were requested or retained.
Packet completion is not source integration/admission.

No independent runtime adapter qualification was performed.
